data.title: Kansas City Fed Services Activity Index Flat in September
data.description:
By Colin Kellaher

Services activity in the middle of the U.S. was flat in September, while expectations for future activity edged higher, according to a monthly survey by the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City.

The Tenth District Services Survey's composite index, a weighted average of indexes covering revenue/sales, employment and inventory, came in at 0 in September, compared with readings of minus 3 in August and 14 in July. Readings above zero indicate expansion, while those below zero indicate contraction.

The Kansas City Fed said consumer services grew moderately in September, driven by increased activity in the transportation sector, while business services fell further.

The bank said its index of expectations for future services activity came in at 12 in September, up from 5 in August.

The Kansas City Fed's survey, released Friday, includes participants from such service industries as retail and wholesale trade, automobile dealers, real estate and restaurants. The survey provides information on current services activity in the Tenth District, which includes Colorado, Oklahoma, Wyoming, Nebraska, Kansas, the northern half of New Mexico and the western third of Missouri.

The bank's monthly manufacturing survey, released Thursday, showed that manufacturing activity in the central U.S. accelerated in September.

Write to Colin Kellaher at colin.kellaher@wsj.com

data.title: AI messaging scam costs Italy's top bank Intesa millions, sources say
data.description:
By Emilio Parodi

Fraudsters using AI to impersonate senior executives stole €95 million ($108 million) from Fideuram, the private banking arm of Italy's biggest lender Intesa Sanpaolo , two sources familiar with the matter said on Friday.

More than half the funds were later recovered, but some €36 million remains missing, the sources said.

The scheme, first reported by Corriere della Sera, began in February when then-Fideuram Chairman Paolo Molesini received what appeared to be a WhatsApp message from Intesa Sanpaolo CEO Carlo Messina seeking urgent help with an overseas transaction.

The fraudsters followed up with a phone call that appeared to come from a senior partner at a prominent law firm, confirming the instruction. According to the sources, the callers used AI technology to replicate the lawyer's voice.

Believing the request was genuine, Molesini instructed his finance department to arrange a series of transfers to foreign accounts, mainly in China and Hong Kong, the sources said.

Intesa Sanpaolo and Fideuram declined to comment.

Fideuram quickly detected irregularities in the transfers and alerted banks and authorities in several countries. Roughly €53 million was later recovered through cooperation between authorities in China, Portugal and Italy, according to the sources.

The remaining funds have not been traced after passing through a network of overseas accounts and being converted into cryptocurrencies, they said.

Neither Molesini nor any other Fideuram executives are under investigation, the sources said. However, Milan prosecutors have placed a foreign national living outside Europe under investigation on suspicion of computer fraud, one of the sources said.

Molesini resigned as chairman in March citing personal reasons. At the time, Fideuram gave no further explanation for his departure.

Last year, fraudsters using AI to mimic the voice of an Italian minister persuaded businessman Massimo Moratti to transfer nearly €1 million to an overseas account. The money was later recovered.

($1 = 0.8772 euros)

data.title: Tesla's stock falls as Semi launch fails to excite investors
data.description:
By William Gavin

Autonomous trucking represents a compelling opportunity for Tesla, but it's unclear what the company's initial Semi targets look like

Volume production of the Tesla Semi officially started on Thursday.

Tesla will finally begin deliveries of its all-electric Semi truck to customers this week, after years of delays.

The heavy-duty Semi was announced by Tesla (TSLA) CEO Elon Musk in November 2017. At the time, the company had plans to kick off production a few years later. However, the company repeatedly pushed back the launch, preventing it from being able to serve the long-haul freight market on its original timeline.

But at an event on Thursday, Tesla executives confirmed that the company's Nevada factory will be capable of producing up to 50,000 Semi trucks each year. The first truck rolled off the high-volume production line in April and volume production officially began Thursday, according to the company.

While it's unclear how many Semi trucks Tesla aims to make or sell this year, the company has attracted orders from customers including PepsiCo (PEP) and DHL (XE:DHL), which tested the Semi in pilot programs. An alliance of shipping companies this week also announced an order for 2,500 of the trucks.

The Semi comes in two versions, Standard Range and Long Range, with the latter able to travel about 500 miles before needing to recharge its battery. The standard version has 325 miles of range. The company has told customers the Long Range version will cost $290,000, according to Electrek.

"This is really going to be a revolutionary truck," Musk said in a prerecorded video on Thursday. He said the waiting list for the Semi "is already pretty significant."

Musk added that Tesla will "in the very near future" make its Full Self-Driving advanced driver-assistance software available for use with the Semi. In July, he said Tesla would focus on developing the driverless software first for the Cybercab robotaxi and its other vehicles, telling investors that he didn't want the Semi to "be a distraction."

Autonomous trucking could be a big opportunity for Tesla, according to Morgan Stanley analyst Andrew Percoco. He thinks the company could generate about $15,000 in recurring software revenue each month for every truck equipped with autonomous-vehicle technology. By 2040, Percoco estimates Tesla could generate $17 billion in software revenue a year from the Semi, assuming it sells well.

The launch of the Semi comes as diesel prices surge. Tesla emphasized that the Semi's cost per mile is much lower than that of traditional heavy-duty trucks.

"We see Semi as an underappreciated avenue for Tesla to expand its autonomy capabilities, with impressive unit economics that support a strong demand outlook," Percoco said in a note to clients on Friday. He has the equivalent of a neutral rating on the stock and called Thursday's event "another step toward commercial rollout."

Tesla shares were down more than 2% in recent action on Friday.

With the Semi event behind it, Tesla has already turned to promoting a planned showcase of the Roadster, an electric sports car that is the result of a collaboration with SpaceX (SPCX), another company run by Musk. That event is scheduled for Oct. 1.

The Roadster was announced alongside the Semi in 2019 and has faced similar delays. Despite enthusiasm among some Tesla fans, the vehicle isn't expected to be a major financial contributor for the company.

Goldman Sachs analyst Mark Delaney recently noted that "absolute demand" will also be limited by the high cost of the Roadster, which has been estimated to be around $250,000. Just a few thousand are expected to be sold per year, experts say.

The "Roadster's near-term significance is principally as a technology and brand showcase," StoneX analyst Mickey Legg said in a note on Friday. The Semi, he added, is the "more consequential revenue opportunity."

-William Gavin

data.title: ICE Canola Midday: Prices Remaining Lower
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures continued to pull back late Friday morning as declines in crude oil are pressuring the vegetable oils.

"There's no joy in Mudville today if you're in the markets," an analyst said.

The analyst added that he's unsure if the November canola contract can remain above C$820 per metric ton for much longer. He said especially with Chicago soyoil in the 67-cent-per-pound range, which takes away strength from canola.

That said, the Chicago soy complex and Malaysian palm oil were to the downside while European rapeseed was mixed.

Most of the Prairies are to be rain-free on Friday, except for the Edmonton area. More rain is forecast over the weekend for southern Manitoba and most of Alberta, while much of Saskatchewan is to remain dry.

Temperatures for Friday are to range from the high-teens to the high 20s Celsius. During the weekend, that's to be in the low to high-teens.

A new August record was set for the canola crush, with Statistics Canada placing it at nearly 1.24 million tonnes.

The Canadian Grain Commission reported canola exports of 43,300 metric tons for the week ended Sept. 20, up from virtually zero during the previous week. Domestic use fell 16.6 per cent at 198,300 metric tons.

The Canadian dollar was holding steady late Friday morning as the loonie at 70.72 U.S. cents, compared with Thursday's close of 70.74.

data.title: Argentina set for near-record farm dollar windfall as global supply shocks lift grain exports
data.description:
By Kylie Madry

Argentina is on track for a near-record farm export windfall next year as strong crop prices, a bumper harvest and supply disruptions in rival exporting regions boost grain shipments and hard-currency inflows, the Rosario grains exchange said in a report on Friday.

The farm sector could bring in about $40 billion in export dollars in 2027, which would be the second-highest annual total on record behind only 2022, according to the report.

  • Farm exports are Argentina's main source of foreign currency, crucial for replenishing central bank reserves, stabilizing the peso and supporting government finances.

  • Rosario projects Argentina's 2026/27 total grain harvest at 156 million metric tons, one of the largest ever.

  • International prices for corn, wheat and soy have been supported by conflict-related supply risks in the Black Sea, where disruption to Russian and Ukrainian exports has tightened availability, the report said.

  • Argentine farmers have benefited from the disruption, the exchange said in a separate report, with corn sales above 1 million tons per week for four straight weeks and wheat export commitments climbing to their highest level in five years for this point in the season.

  • Demand out of Asia has been notable, with buyers such as Indonesia turning to Argentine crops.

  • Rosario also said export tax revenue from grains and byproducts could rise to $5.48 billion in 2027, up 16% from this year, even though tax rates are due to decline.

data.title: As savings shift to MFs, fund houses must step up to the challenge
data.description:
Welcome Abakkus Asset Manager Ltd to the capital markets in yet another avatar. The Sunil Banwarilal Singhania-promoted fund house recently filed its Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) with capital markets regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its Initial Public Offering (IPO). The IPO is primarily aimed at enabling the company to list its equity shares on the stock exchanges, the fund house said in a release.

As of August end, the fund house is managing assets under management of ₹52,609 crore.

According to an ICRA report cited in the DRHP, Abakkus is among the fastest-growing India-focused asset management platforms in terms of non-mutual fund quarterly average assets under management (QAAUM). Its non-mutual fund QAAUM grew at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 18.39 per cent between FY24 and FY26.

A slew of IPOs

This is the second fund house to enter the IPO market after industry leader SBI Funds Management that launched its public issue in July, raising ₹9,813 crore.

In July, SBI Funds Management — India’s largest asset management company, with assets under management exceeding ₹12 lakh crore — launched its ₹9,813-crore IPO and successfully listed its shares. Earlier, Canara Bank-owned Canara Robeco AMC had also tapped the capital market and listed successfully last year.

Nippon India Mutual Fund (formerly Reliance Mutual Fund, which had earlier acquired Goldman Sachs’ India AMC business) was the first asset management company in India to tap the capital markets, raising ₹1,540 crore through its IPO at issue price of ₹252. If Abakkus lists its shares, it would be the 10th company from the AMC space to enter the listed space directly.

Currently there are 60 AMCs, per SEBI data. They manage over ₹87 lakh crore in assets under management (AUM) as of end August, according to Association of Mutual Funds in India. MF assets have been growing at 18-19 per cent CAGR since FY21. During the same period, the unique investor count in the industry has grown from 5.36 crore to 6.14 crore. Monthly systematic investment plan (SIP) inflows rose to record ₹32,297 crore.

Surging SIPs

One of the major reasons behind the interest in MFs is household investments shifting from bank to MF industry.

“The share of mutual funds in gross flow of annual household savings rose from 3 per cent in 2020 to 13 per cent in 2025, signalling a structural shift in how savings are being intermediated,” said Crisil Intelligence. Rapid digitalisation, higher financial literacy and a preference for systematic investment plans (SIPs) drove this growth, highlighting a shift in investor preferences towards diversified and high-growth investment avenues, the study highlighted.

The buoyancy in the mutual fund industry has also found its way into the stock market, with several listed AMCs delivering stellar returns. Nippon AMC, for instance, has surged 165 per cent over the past five years, far outpacing the Nifty’s 40 per cent gain. Over three years, it has risen 46 per cent, nearly three times the benchmark’s 13 per cent return.

ICICI Prudential and HDFC AMC have also beaten the Nifty, while UTI Mutual Fund has outperformed the benchmark over the past year. In contrast, SBI Funds Management and Canara Robeco Mutual Fund continue to trade below their IPO prices.

Going ahead, the mutual fund space is expected to remain vibrant, with India’s relatively low MF penetration at around 20 per cent of GDP leaving ample room for growth, particularly when compared with developed markets.

However, with more players entering the fray, the AMC space is getting increasingly crowded — not just with fund houses, but also with PMS providers. In this competitive landscape, the ability to innovate — both in products and marketing — will be key to standing out and driving growth. Besides, regulatory changes will remain a key factor to watch closely. Fund houses will need to navigate these challenges while continuing to cater to the growing pool of investors who are increasingly turning to mutual funds over traditional savings avenues.

data.title: Carlyle completes strategic majority stake acquisition in Nido Home Finance
data.description:
Carlyle Asia Partners has completed its purchase of a majority stake in Nido Home Finance by investing over ₹2,000 crore through a mix of primary capital infusion and secondary share purchase, marking one of the largest private equity bets in India’s affordable housing finance sector this year. The deal, first announced in February 2026, was closed after obtaining all regulatory and statutory approvals.

The primary capital infusion totals around ₹1,450 crore, of which approximately ₹725 crore has already been received, while the balance will be infused over the next 18 months. Separately, Carlyle has completed the purchase of a 45 per cent stake from Edelweiss for about ₹600 crore. Following the completion of the capital infusion, Edelweiss will retain roughly 26 per cent ownership in Nido on a fully diluted basis.

The fresh capital is expected to nearly triple Nido’s net worth to around ₹2,300 crore over the next 18 months, significantly strengthening its balance sheet and lending capacity. Established in 2010, Nido is among India’s leading housing finance companies focused on affordable and mid-income housing markets. The company serves more than 800 talukas across the country and managed assets under management of approximately ₹4,900 crore as of June 2026.

For Edelweiss, the transaction represents a key value-unlocking initiative, enabling it to monetise part of its stake, reduce debt and bring in a global long-term investor to support the next stage of Nido’s growth. The company said the partnership would provide Nido with growth capital and access to Carlyle’s operational expertise as it expands deeper into underserved rural, semi-urban and emerging markets.

Carlyle’s investment also marks a significant bet on India’s housing finance sector, which continues to benefit from strong structural demand. The global investment firm has a longstanding presence in India and an established track record in financial services through investments in entities such as YES Bank, SBI Card and SBI Life. Carlyle managed $477 billion in assets as of December 31, 2025.

The transaction is being led by Sunil Kaul, Partner and Asia Financial Services Sector Lead at Carlyle, while Aditya Puri, former Managing Director of HDFC Bank and now a Senior Advisor to Carlyle, is also participating as an investor through Salisbury Investments Pvt Ltd.

The deal is expected to position Nido for its next phase of growth, enhancing its ability to expand customer reach, strengthen its market position and deepen its presence in India’s affordable housing finance segment.

data.title: West Bengal govt to auction limited parcels to industry associations
data.description:
The West Bengal government will offer land parcels through a limited auction procedure to industry associations for the setting up of specific product-based industrial parks in the State.

“Whatever land parcel we have in our hand, we would like to offer it to the chambers of commerce and to the industry associations for the setting up of specific product-based industrial parks according to your requirement,” said Subrata Gupta, Chief Advisor to the Chief Minister, during the fourth edition of the Indo-Pacific Economic Conclave on the occasion of industry body BCCI’s 172nd Annual General Meeting.

“Instead of the government trying to develop these parks, we would like the industry associations to develop the parks, and we will facilitate them. This is one of the initiatives which the State government is taking,” Gupta said.

The government has already identified three-four land parcels which would be handed over to industry bodies through a limited auction procedure.

Proposed land policy

Commenting on the proposed land policy, likely to be unveiled in October, Gupta said the government is also considering land pooling. “In some States like Haryana and Gujarat, land pooling policy is very successful. We have to see how it would works here if it is rolled out,” he added.

Earlier this week, the government handed over around 580 acres of land for 33 industrial projects. These projects have to be completed within three years. The 33 projects entail a total investment of around ₹60,000 crore, and have the potential to generate nearly 62,000 jobs.

Around 256 acres of land was allotted to Jupiter Defence in the State’s Purulia district for a large-scale and state-of-the-art integrated defence manufacturing facility.

The government also allotted around 54.20 acres to Websol Energy System at Falta Industrial Park, located near Kolkata, for its planned greenfield solar manufacturing facility. The new facility is planned to have 4 GW of solar cell capacity and 4 GW of solar module manufacturing capacity, to be developed in two phases of 2GW each.

data.title: Runwal Enterprises, German Green Steel and Power raise ₹149 crore, ₹91 crore from anchor investors
data.description:
Friday saw four companies tapping the capital market with initial public offerings (IPOs) that robust-to-moderate interest from investors.

Among them, the issues from German Green Steel and Orient Cables (India) were fully subscribed on Day 1 itself, while Runwal Enterprises and Ace Vector saw a modest response.

Ahead of the IPOs, Runwal Enterprises and German Green Steel and Power raised ₹149 crore and ₹91 crore from anchor investors; AceVector, the parent company of Snapdeal, Unicommerce and Stellaro Brands, raised ₹189 crore, while Gurugram-based Orient Cables mopped up ₹165.6 crore.

Runwal Enterprises, the real estate firm, allocated 48,83,605 shares at ₹305 a share to anchor investors, including Tata Mutual Fund, 360 One Prime, Maybank Securities Pte, Authum Investment And Infrastructure and Mukul Agarwal backed Sanshi Fund-I, Madhu Kela backed Founders Collective Fund, Capri Global Capital, Ashika Global Finance and LRSD Securities (which was identified as a person acting in concert with Rajasthan Global Securities founded by Lalit Dua) also participated in the anchor book.

Runwal Enterprises has fixed the price band as ₹290-305. The company will make fresh share issuance of ₹500 crore. Out of the IPO proceeds, the company will use ₹100 crore for repayment of debt and park ₹225 crore in wholly owned subsidiaries for repayment of borrowing, funding acquisitions of future real estate projects and general corporate purpose.

At the end of Day 1, the IPO was subscribed 0.42 time.

German Green Steel and Power, a vertically integrated iron and steel manufacturer, garnered ₹91 crore from anchor investors. It has allocated 65.59 lakh shares at ₹139 a share to anchor investors.

Marquee investors

Some of the marquee institutions that participated in the anchor include Necta Bloom VCC – Necta Bloom One, Lords Multigrowth Fund, Compact Structure Fund, Arnesta Global Opportunities Fund PCC – Arnesta Global Fund 1, Zeal Global Opportunities Fund and Venus Investments VCC – Venus Stellar Fund.

German Green Steel and Power Ltd has fixed the price band of ₹132-139 a share. The IPO consists of a fresh issue of ₹290 crore and an offer for sale for up to 10 lakh shares by promoters. The IPO was subscribed 1.73 times.

The IPO of Oriental Cables was subscribed 1.96 times while that of Ace Vector 0.23 times.

data.title: Blue Cloud arm bags $15.5 million order from IBM Cloud
data.description:
Global Impx Inc (GIX), an arm of Blue Cloud Softech Solutions Ltd has bagged an order worth $15.5 million (about ₹147 crore) from IBM Cloud Inc for AI infrastructure design, deployment and support services.

Work on the order began on September 24, and the fee will be paid after fixed milestones. In this engagement, GIX will deliver a scalable, secure, high-performance environment for the client’s AI and machine learning workloads, covering model development, training, fine-tuning and inference.

The work would include assessing AI workloads and existing infrastructure, followed by high-level architecture and detailed design, and building GPU compute clusters, high-performance storage, and networking.

“AI is moving out of the lab and into production, and that move runs on infrastructure. Winning this mandate from IBM Cloud within three months of GIX joining Blue Cloud shows that our US platform can compete for, and deliver, the most demanding AI infrastructure work,” Tejesh Kumar Kodali, Group Chairman, Blue Cloud Softech Solutions Ltd, said in a statement on Friday.

data.title: Infosys nears July lows, Wipro hits fresh 52-week low
data.description:
Infosys slipped below ₹1,000 for the second time this year and Wipro hit a fresh low, even as the broader market ticked higher but remains on track for a seventh straight weekly decline.

India’s information technology stocks remained under pressure on Friday, with large-cap names such as Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Coforge and Mphasis ending lower as investors continued to reassess the sector’s growth prospects amid rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and broader market uncertainty.

Infosys and Oracle Financial Services Software (OFSS) was among the worst performers. Infosys slipped below ₹1,000 for the second time this year to ₹998, levels last seen on July 1.

While TCS declined 0.24 per cent. Mid-tier IT firms Coforge and Mphasis also came under selling pressure. Wipro, despite featuring among the gainers during the session, touched a fresh 52-week low of ₹161.66, falling below its previous July trough.

Volatile market

The weakness in IT stocks comes against the backdrop of a volatile market environment. The Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex recovered modestly on Friday after Thursday’s sharp sell-off, rising 0.34 per cent and 0.43 per cent respectively. However, both benchmarks still recorded their seventh consecutive weekly decline, the longest losing streak since 2020, as investors grappled with elevated crude oil prices, rising global bond yields and geopolitical tensions.

The pain has been more pronounced in technology stocks than in the broader market. The Nifty IT index has fallen about 21.5 per cent over the past year, compared with an around 8 per cent decline in the Nifty 50. Over the last six months, Nifty IT has slipped about 2.4 per cent, underperforming the benchmark index’s nearly 1.8 per cent fall, reflecting investor concerns over slowing technology spending and the industry’s transition to AI-led business models.

“Indian companies are not seen as proxies to the AI companies. They are still considered in the brick-and-mortar business. Yet, management of the companies are building AI capacities and upskilling employees in last few quarters. Therefore, even though Infosys is attractive in terms of valuations, it is a contrarian move to invest in the large-caps. The next coming quarters and years will be crucial for all companies with regards to AI,” said Kranthi Bathini, Director, Equity Strategy at WealthMills Securities.

Previous disruptions

Bathini, however, noted that Indian IT companies have successfully navigated previous disruptions, including the 2008 global financial crisis and the Covid-19 pandemic, demonstrating their ability to adapt during periods of economic stress.

Industry executives also remain optimistic about the sector’s longer-term prospects. Speaking at the SBI Banking and Economics Conclave, Rahul Singh, Chief Operating Officer of HCL Technologies, stressed the industry’s ability to weather the AI-driven transformation. He said the sector is evolving towards an outcome-based pricing model, marking a significant shift from the traditional manpower-led billing structure.

“Our pricing models have to change, our clients have to develop trust in terms of being able to accept all the outputs that we produce. As the industry pivots to that, the markets will self-correct and we will heal over time,” Singh said.

data.title: Sundaram Home Finance aims to double emerging biz disbursements in Central TN
data.description:
Sundaram Home Finance is expanding its presence in the Emerging Business (EB) segment in small towns in central Tamil Nadu.

The company, which opened a new branch in Mannargudi on Friday, is targeting to almost double disbursements in this segment to nearly ₹200 crore in Central TN this year. The company is also looking to open EB branches in Karaikkal and Thiruthuraipoondi in the near future.

Sundaram Home Finance currently has close to 25 EB branches in Central TN in small towns such as Kumbakonam, Manapparai, Aranthangi, Pudukottai and Pattukottai, in addition to a presence in larger towns such as Trichy and Thanjavur.

The Emerging Business segment comprises of working capital loans of up to ₹20 lakh and affordable housing finance of up to ₹40 lakh.

D. Lakshminarayanan, MD, Sundaram Home Finance said, “Small towns are driving our growth in the Emerging Business segment. Our current expansion is in line with our strategy of penetrating deep into small towns and establishing a strong presence in Tier-3 and 4 towns in the EB segment.”

Sundaram Home Finance has over 100 branches in the Emerging Business segment spread across TN, Karnataka, Andhra and Telangana.

data.title: JSW One Platforms moves SEBI for ₹3,054-cr IPO
data.description:
JSW One Platforms, a B2B commerce player promoted by the JSW Group and backed by Mitsui, has filed a draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the SEBI for a ₹3,054-crore IPO. The offer comprises a fresh issue worth ₹1,300 crore and an offer-for-sale of ₹1,754 crore. JSW Steel Ltd, JSW Cement Ltd and Mitsui & Co will offload part of their stake through the OFS window in the IPO.

The company proposes to utilise the net proceeds towards investment in JSW One Distribution Ltd (JODL) for marketing and brand-building expenditure, technology and platform development expenditure, investment in JSW One Finance Ltd (JOFL) to augment its capital base and general corporate purposes. Besides, ₹125 crore will be invested in JODL and ₹500 crore in JOFL, while up to ₹350 crore is proposed towards technology and platform development.

JSW One Platforms operates an integrated digital platform connecting MSMEs with sellers of manufacturing and construction materials, while bringing together commerce, embedded financing, logistics, processing and customisation and private brands. As of June 30, 2026, the platform had 95,611 registered customers, 165 cumulative brands and 1,713 sellers, with its network spanning 6,963 serviceable pin codes, supported by 81 logistics partners, 12 contract service centres and 9 contract manufacturers.

JM Financial Ltd, Kotak Mahindra Capital Company Ltd, ICICI Securities Ltd, SBI Capital Markets Ltd and PL Capital Markets Private Ltd are the book-running lead managers to the offer. KFin Technologies Ltd is the Registrar to the offer.

data.title: BMW i5 eDrive 35L: New India-made luxury EV with strong value
data.description:
The i5 isn’t a new name to India. In 2024, BMW did give us a flavour of what it could do with an EV sedan, courtesy of the i5 M60, which was less car, more rocket. The i5 you see here isn’t the same or anywhere close. This i5 eDrive 35L is a made-in-India long-wheelbase sedan that attempts to package luxury, electric economy and hard-to-ignore pricing to settle its age-old rivalry with the Mercedes-Benz E-Class.

In doing so, the i5, in fact, threatens its own kin. You can have one for ₹79.60 lakh, which makes it exactly ₹3 lakh more expensive than the petrol-engined 530Li M Sport, priced at ₹76.60 lakh. The most affordable E-Class, the E 200 LWB, is priced at ₹81.50 lakh (all prices, ex-showroom). What this will translate to across dealerships is tough to predict — we are in an SUV-dominated market, after all — but what this context-setting exercise indicates is BMW’s intent. Cars across classes, however, are sought after for more than mere objectivity. Does the i5 do anything to stir your soul?

It does, but in a very different way to what you’d usually expect from a BMW. The i5 is no purist’s dream; BMW would rather you looked elsewhere in its range for driving thrills. The electrified 5 Series has been relieved of that responsibility for its own good. It’s a tough one to swallow and yet perfectly rational.

LONG STORY

Let’s get to the specifics. In this spec, the i5 now measures 5175 mm in length and features a 3105 mm wheelbase. That makes it longer than any of its peers, and it sure looks it, too. There’s an almost SUV-like stance to it with its near-vertical front end, and the bonnet appears long enough to be able to accommodate a 16-cylinder engine under it.

It’s a struggle to call it pretty, but it looks striking and impressive, with its tight shutlines, impeccable surface finishes and decided modernity. The sheer expanse of its bodywork makes its 20-inch wheels look just right, a good departure from the 18s on the ICE 5. There isn’t enough to tell you it’s an EV, though, aside from a tiny ‘i’ badge integrated into one of the kidney ‘grille’ elements and an i5 badge on the boot lid. Even the beautiful satin-aluminium garnish at the base of the C-pillar just says ‘5’.

The interior is beautifully minimalist, firmly upmarket and understated. The twin-curved-screen setup looks modern, and the diffused ambient light strips across the dash and door panels give it a perfectly contemporary edge. The open-pore trim on the dash looks premium, too, and the layered centre console, with its crystal-finish drive selector and dial, looks and feels terrific. Beyond the centre console is a sea of tan leather — could’ve been darker, perhaps — that’s a bit old-school but well-finished nonetheless.

The seats in both row are brilliant, too. The front row is comfortable, with an elaborate backrest and seatbase, adjustable to a great degree. There’s an ever-so-slight hint of sportiness to them, which bodes well for when (for whatever reason) you’re in the mood for an upbeat drive. The backseat is, of course, where the i5 wants to excel — and it does. This is a sublime backseat, a great place to conduct business-y things or just to stretch out after a hard day in the office. The floor does seat you slightly knees-up given the battery pack underneath, but it’s far from a deal-breaker.

What it lacks is a recline function and a ‘boss’ mode that lets you push the co-driver’s seat away to create extra room, both of which are available on the E-Class. It also misses sun shades (again, present on the E) for the rear windows, which tells you just how stretched BMW was in trying to price the i5 in the way it has. The boot, while spacious by design, features a spare wheel right on the boot floor itself, which means you’ll struggle to fit hard luggage — not an ideal car to be chauffeured to the airport in, then. This, by the way, isn’t the case with the ICE 5 Series, which features its spare under the boot floor.

ON A CHARGE

That aside, it’s comfortably one of the strongest-configured BMWs out there. Featuring an 81.6 kWh battery pack and a single rear-mounted motor, the i5’s powertrain produces 268 bhp and 41.8 kg-m, good enough to keep its performance nearly level with its petrol counterpart. The claimed range is 669 km, although under a mixed driving cycle and drawing from the indicated data from our short stint with it, a real-world range of 450 km or so should be possible. With DC fast charging (capable of up to 160 kW), you can charge it from 10-80 per cent in 33 minutes (claimed), which is really impressive for its use case.

To drive, the i5 is a surprise package. Okay, it’s no pocket rocket, but having evolved from the textbook definition of what a 5 Series had to be, its spiritedness is rather stately. In ‘Sport’ mode, the i5 can produce strong acceleration all the way to its 195-kph limited top speed, but you’ll rarely want to drive it in that frame of mind. Here’s a BMW that offers brilliant real-world performance; overtakes are quick and easy, and you’ll take off from traffic lights (or toll gates) with agility. It isn’t, however, a driver’s car and that’s probably all right. The steering, for one, is too light — great for city driving — but bears no resemblance to anything its lineage represents. I wish it had some heft, even if electronically induced, because it’s slightly tricky to judge at really high speeds.

Where BMW shows its strengths, especially as a formidable EV maker, is in the calibration of everything. The throttle, for one, is clearly the new benchmark in how connected and communicative it feels. Yes, the inherent silence is a dead giveaway of the i5 being an EV, but to drive it feels no different from driving an ICE car. It takes virtually no time at all to adapt to its mannerisms, and, especially thanks to the four regen levels (Low, Mid, High and Adaptive), you can drive the i5 in a way you wouldn’t expect to drive a car of its dimensions. There’s a ‘B’ mode, too, which is its done-to-perfection single-pedal driving mode.

What you’ll love about it, regardless of whether you choose to drive or be chauffeured, is its ride quality. You’d think a heavy, low-slung sedan with 20-inch wheels would come with compromises, but the i5 is just phenomenal in its ability to soak up road undulations. Ground clearance is surprisingly good, too, and even the trickiest of speed breakers posed no challenge for it. This, along with a well-insulated cabin, translates to a 5 Series-like experience, unlike any before it.

At ₹79.60 lakh, the i5 goes beyond just compelling. Provided its feature omissions don’t matter to you, the i5 sets a solid standard for what you can expect from a luxury sedan. As an EV, it has capabilities rather than limitations, and it works brilliantly as a modern, large and plush machine. Take a bow, BMW!

@TheMotorGram

data.title: After two overseas buys, Poly Medicure doubles down on domestic manufacturing
data.description:
With two overseas acquisitions in the bag, medical devices maker Poly Medicure is focussing on shoring up its domestic manufacturing in segments including cardiac and orthopaedic products.

“So every year, the plan is [for] the next four years, by FY30, we plan to launch 25, 30 new products every year,” said Himanshu Baid, Managing Director, Poly Medicure Ltd, adding that the focus would be on cardiac, orthopaedic, nephrology, gastro, and oncology products.

“We have around 390 patents …and we are working on a lot of new technologies, a lot of new devices, which we are trying to bring in. And most of these technologies are import substitution. So that is further going to help hospitals save costs and…. reduce our dependency on foreign technology and foreign products,” Baid told businessline.

Late last year, Poly Medicure inked agreements to wholly acquire Italy-based Citieffe Group at an enterprise value of ₹324 crore; besides a majority stake in Netherlands-based PendraCare Group at an enterprise value of ₹188.5 crore. While Citieffe makes orthopaedic trauma products, PendraCare specialises in cardiology ancillary consumables, besides developing and manufacturing cardiology catheter solutions.

New facilities

“We’re transferring some of the production to India. And this will help us to lower the cost,” he said. The integration following the two acquisitions were complete, Baid said, adding that nothing changes for the employees. However, all the additional capacity would come up in India, he said, of new facilities in Haryana, and a second in the medical park in Uttar Pradesh.

About 70 percent of the company’s ₹1875-crore revenues are from exports. But increased freight, plastics and insurance costs, and challenges of the Hormuz and Red Sea shipping routes, besides US tariffs were adding to the unpredictability hanging over the sector, he said. Presently, as the second largest medical device company in the country, he said, they expected to close the financial year with a turnover of about ₹2,300 crore.
